scope: Three historically unresolved Upper Peninsula waterfall research entries; current-season land-manager access crosschecks. No destinations or pins are authorized.
status: PARTIAL: confirmed adjacent trails, water approaches and wilderness management; complete waterfall-viewpoint routes remain unverified.
qualityRules: A published trail or portage elsewhere in the same drainage is NOT automatically a signed trail to a waterfall.
Do not infer tourism waterfalls share GNIS or secondary-directory GPS points without official identity support.
Do not substitute protected-land boundaries or public general foot access for an independently documented continuous approach.
Do not transfer Wisconsin Siskiwit directions to Isle Royale.
Source-only waterfall records retain null coordinates; no parking pins, route lines or new public travel cards.
Seasonal park closure is an annually recurring rule, not a fresh availability feed; sources should be revisited before publication as current.

records.landManager: Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
records.asOfAccess: FEDERAL FEATURE IDENTITIES DISTINCT; DNR TRAIL PROXIMITY COMPUTED; UNNAMED WATERFALL IDENTITY AND VIEWPOINT ROUTES UNVERIFIED
records.shortVerdict: USGS directly confirms Pinkerton Falls (GNIS 2126322) and Traders Falls (GNIS 1615029) as distinct named features, approximately 1.97 km apart. A DNR backcountry map labels Traders Falls. The separately unnamed UP Travel cascade is still NOT uniquely identified, and there is no verified continuous waterfall-viewpoint route.
records.seasonality: Michigan DNR reports the South Boundary Road section serving the Pinkerton Trailhead closes to vehicles December 1 through late spring; this is a recurring policy, not a live road-status feed.

officialFacts.fact: USGS October 2026 Gazetteer separately lists Pinkerton Falls (GNIS 2126322) and Traders Falls (GNIS 1615029), both Gogebic County natural features classified as Falls; federal points are approximately 1,971 m apart.

Michigan DNR public hiking-trail GIS returns 66 approved, nonmotorized-Open Pinkerton Trail segment records totaling approximately 2.434 mapped miles. The closest GIS trail segment is approximately 364 m from the USGS Pinkerton Falls point and 70 m from the USGS Traders Falls point. These are map proximities, NOT walkable routes or trail closures.

A DNR-hosted Porcupine Mountains detailed backcountry map labels Traders Falls in the Pinkerton Trail area; it does not establish a signed waterfall-viewpoint spur or identify the unrelated unnamed UP Travel drop.
DNR's 2.6-mile Pinkerton Trail description divides South Boundary Road to Pinkerton Creek (1.4 miles) and Pinkerton Creek to Lake Superior Trail (1.2 miles).
DNR trail description identifies the creek crossing, not a signed waterfall spur or named Pinkerton Falls viewpoint.
DNR posts a seasonal vehicle closure on the park's South Boundary Road to the Pinkerton Trailhead beginning December 1 and lasting until late spring.

independentFacts.fact: A Western U.P. waterfall brochure published in an April 2026 source location gives a Traders Falls point that differs by approximately 318 m from the USGS official Traders Falls point, despite being only about 37 m from DNR Pinkerton Trail geometry. It is useful context, not federal location authority.

Another independently published directory supplies Pinkerton Falls coordinates approximately 5.0 km from the federal point, and Traders Falls coordinates approximately 16.4 km from its federal point. These contradictory locations are rejected as destination/map pins.
UP Travel describes an unnamed Pinkerton Creek cascade and an improved-trail time estimate without a separately verified natural-feature identification.

Independent name compilations mention Pinkerton Falls in Gogebic County and associate a USGS GNIS identifier with the named feature; another independent travel directory also describes Traders Falls on Pinkerton Creek. These names do not prove the tourism listing describes the same drop.

records.establishedStart: Michigan DNR explicitly maps the approved Pinkerton Hiking Trail and describes a 2.6-mile trail with a creek crossing 1.4 miles from South Boundary Road. The public GIS geometry's 66 segments sum to 2.434 miles, a different map measurement. Neither is a verified walk to Pinkerton Falls or Traders Falls; seasonal road access restrictions apply.
records.waterfallViewpoint: No DNR-approved continuous pedestrian route from the trail to a signed Pinkerton Falls viewpoint or precise Traders Falls viewpoint was verified. Approximate federal geographic-name points are 364 and 70 straight-line meters from the mapped trail, respectively. The unnamed UP Travel cascade lacks an official named-feature join.
records.falseEquivalence: The two USGS-named natural waterfalls are CONFIRMED DISTINCT by separate GNIS feature IDs and coordinates about 1.97 km apart. UP Travel's unnamed cascade may or may not correspond to either; do not equate it with both, infer an off-trail spur, or treat Traders' trail proximity as public arrival.
nextEvidence: An official park source or surveyed evidence explicitly identifying the UP Travel 'Unnamed Falls on Pinkerton Creek' as federal Pinkerton Falls, Traders Falls, or a separately named/unnamed drop.
An official continuous legal pedestrian viewpoint trail/management statement for either of the two named falls; 70 m and 364 m GIS proximity values are not a hiking route.
Current approved parking, route/trail conditions and South Boundary Road access for a specific visit; DNR GIS 'Open' is not live recreation availability.

records.landManager: USDA Forest Service, Ottawa National Forest (McCormick Wilderness)
records.shortVerdict: The federal land manager confirms cascades on the designated upper Yellow Dog River and foot access to McCormick Wilderness. It does NOT publish a signed trail and continuous waterfall approach specifically to Bulldog Falls.
records.seasonality: Wilderness is not a signed day-use attraction; check federal forest alerts and road/bridge conditions before any independent wilderness excursion.

officialFacts.fact: Federal Wild and Scenic River designation covers the Yellow Dog River from the Bulldog Lake Dam outlet to the Ottawa National Forest boundary. Federal source describes multiple cascades and a cumulative river drop, not a single Bulldog Falls height.

The USFS McCormick Wilderness brochure documents the three-mile White Deer Lake Trail, while the rest of the wilderness is rugged and difficult to access; that trail is NOT an official marked route to Bulldog Falls.

The Ottawa National Forest recreation guide describes McCormick access on foot and warns that wilderness trails/intersections may be unsigned or difficult to identify; apparent paths can be user-created/animal traces.

independentFacts.fact: A waterfall field account describes a cascade series below Bulldog Lake with an informal approach involving creek crossings and an old footbridge. These are historic independent observations, not a current Forest Service maintained trail.

A separate Yellow Dog River Community Forest has a land-manager-promoted signed parking area and trail to Hills Falls; it is a different Yellow Dog River waterfall system and does NOT solve access to Bulldog Falls.

records.establishedStart: The Forest Service documents McCormick Wilderness foot access and its separate White Deer Lake Trail; neither is an agency-approved start-to-falls itinerary.
records.waterfallViewpoint: No USDA Forest Service named Bulldog Falls trailhead, signed waterfall spur, mapped continuous route, safe stream crossing or maintained viewing area was verified.
records.falseEquivalence: Do not substitute the Yellow Dog River Community Forest's marked Hills Falls parking/trail, the generic West Yellow Dog Falls entry, or the White Deer Lake Trail for a Bulldog Falls visit.
nextEvidence: Forest Service-authored and current McCormick Wilderness trail/road access description specifically connecting a legal start to the Bulldog cascade reach.
Current land-manager confirmation of route status and stream-crossing safety for a specific waterfall viewpoint (if any).
A named-feature identity match without using third-party GPS for public-arrival links.

records.landManager: National Park Service, Isle Royale National Park
records.asOfAccess: PARK SEASONALLY CLOSED ON REVIEW DATE; official water-access corridors only within annual open season
records.accessVerdict: PARK CLOSED NOVEMBER 1–APRIL 15; NO VERIFIED FALLS ROUTE
records.shortVerdict: NPS's 2026 Greenstone confirms the 0.3-mile Malone Bay–Siskiwit Lake canoe portage and an authorized Malone Bay campground/dock. Neither establishes a marked viewpoint trail to Siskiwit Falls.
records.seasonality: NPS annually closes all park islands to public use November 1 through April 15. As reviewed November 8, 2026, that closure is in effect. Reopening eligibility begins April 16, subject to current conditions and transport.

officialFacts.fact: NPS 2026 Greenstone lists Malone Bay–Siskiwit Lake canoe portage 0.3 mile with approximately 40 feet of slope; this is a portage to a lake, not an advertised waterfall trail.
NPS identifies Malone Bay campground/dock as accessible by foot, canoe, kayak or private boat, with limited services, not by road.
The Voyageur II ferry stops at Malone Bay only when passenger drop-offs or pickups are arranged in advance; a published stop does not guarantee a direct same-day waterfall visit.
NPS Superintendent's Compendium and operating-hours page establish annual island closure November 1 through April 15. On November 8, 2026 the island is closed to public use.

independentFacts.fact: UP Travel names Siskiwit Falls near the outlet of Siskiwit Lake toward Malone Bay. The tourist source is not a current NPS-published signed waterfall viewpoint or trail.
Bayfield County, Wisconsin manages a DIFFERENT Siskiwit Falls trail near Cornucopia. Its parking/trail information does not apply to Isle Royale.

records.establishedStart: NPS publishes the Malone Bay dock/campground and an official portage to Siskiwit Lake, when the park is open. The portage is a supported access corridor, not a confirmed route to a waterfall viewpoint.
records.waterfallViewpoint: No NPS-established footpath or direct managed viewing route connecting the Malone Bay–Siskiwit Lake portage to the named Siskiwit Falls was verified; no official trail length-to-falls or permitted waterfall-specific stop can be claimed.
records.falseEquivalence: The 0.3-mile NPS portage is NOT the 'distance to Siskiwit Falls'; a Wisconsin Siskiwit Falls trailhead or parking address is not on Isle Royale.
nextEvidence: An NPS map, trail description or park publication explicitly placing Siskiwit Falls on a managed pedestrian route with an accessible waterfall viewpoint.
Official seasonal access confirmation and transport/reservation evidence for an intended open-season visit, without assuming ferry departures or weather.
Land-manager waterfall-specific hazard and trail conditions, including whether a viewpoint is on an established portage or would require off-trail navigation.
